skill.name: industry-key-contact-radar-api-skill
skill.description: Finds public professional profiles and contact-related details for industry and role searches through the BrowserAct hosted workflow API.
skill.summary: Runs BrowserAct contact discovery for role, industry, site, and result-limit searches.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The review found expected BrowserAct network calls and intended local script execution, plus unsafe credential-handling guidance. The most important issue is that the skill tells users to provide an API key in chat, and the lead-generation workflow has privacy and anti-abuse concerns. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that ask users to provide API keys in chat. Require BROWSERACT_API_KEY through an environment variable or approved secret manager.
Add guardrails that limit use to lawful public data, site terms, consent requirements, and opt-out obligations.
Disclose that search parameters, task data, and authentication are sent to BrowserAct APIs before users run the workflow.
Document exact command arguments, validate result limits and target sites, and advise users to review scripts before running them.

content.value_statement: Finding public decision-maker profiles across sites can be slow and inconsistent. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow that returns names, profile links, introductions, and company context.
actual_capabilities: Runs the BrowserAct Industry Key Contact Radar workflow from a local Python script.
Searches by industry, target site, job title, and maximum result count.
Polls task status until finished, failed, canceled, or timed out.
Prints returned profile URLs, names, introductions, and company associations.
Handles missing, invalid, or concurrency-limited API keys with user-facing messages.
limitations: Requires a valid BROWSERACT_API_KEY and network access to BrowserAct.
Results depend on BrowserAct availability and target site search visibility.
It does not verify identity, consent, or outreach compliance.
Long-running tasks can take several minutes and may time out.

use_cases.title: Sales Prospecting
use_cases.description: Build a small list of public founder or executive profiles for a defined industry and site.

use_cases.title: Recruiting Research
use_cases.description: Find public profiles for growth, marketing, or leadership roles before manual review.

use_cases.title: Market Mapping
use_cases.description: Identify visible leaders and company associations across competitor or sector searches.

prompt_templates.title: Find Founders
prompt_templates.prompt: Find 10 founder profiles in browser automation on LinkedIn using this skill. Summarize names, profile links, introductions, and companies.

prompt_templates.title: Target Role and Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BrowserAct to search healthcare on facebook.com for marketing manager profiles. Limit results to 15 and flag missing company details.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Run separate searches for CEO and growth leader profiles in e-commerce on linkedin.com. Compare patterns in companies and introductions.

prompt_templates.title: Build Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Search three target industries for founder profiles on linkedin.com, keep each run to 10 results, remove duplicates, and prepare an outreach research brief.

output_examples.input: Search browser automation for founders on LinkedIn.
output_examples.output: A contact research summary with public profile links, names, introductions, company context, and task status notes.

output_examples.input: Find marketing managers in healthcare on Facebook.
output_examples.output: A reviewed list of matching public profiles, with missing company details clearly marked for manual follow-up.

output_examples.input: Compare CEO and growth leader profiles in e-commerce.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of visible roles, company patterns, repeated profiles, and recommended records to verify manually.

best_practices: Use only public profile searches and respect terms for each site and applicable privacy laws.
Store the BrowserAct API key in an environment variable or approved secret manager.
Review returned contacts manually before outreach, enrichment, or recruiting decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into chat or saved prompts.
Do not use the skill to collect private, sensitive, or non-consensual data.
Do not run broad scraping jobs without a clear business purpose and compliance review.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY to be set as an environment variable before running the script.

faq.question: Which sites can it search?
faq.answer: The target site is user supplied, such as LinkedIn, Facebook, or GitHub, subject to BrowserAct support and site rules.

faq.question: Does it guarantee contact accuracy?
faq.answer: No. It returns workflow results that should be verified before outreach, hiring, or analysis decisions.

faq.question: Can it find private contact information?
faq.answer: It is intended for public profile research only and should not be used to seek private or sensitive data.

faq.question: How long does a run take?
faq.answer: Runs can take several minutes. The script polls status and times out after about 15 minutes.

faq.question: What should users do with the results?
faq.answer: Users should verify each result, document a lawful purpose, and follow outreach, recruiting, and privacy requirements.
